newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight rates dip in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight rates dip in liquid market.

text.p: * Volume thins to 12.350 billion pesos from 14.451 billion
Manila overnight money dipped to an average of 10.8125 percent on Wednesday from 10.84375 amid ample liquidity in the market, traders said.
Done rates were wedged between 11 and 10.78125 percent, with 22 borrowers and 17 lenders in the market.
"Banks are now trying to invest their funds but they are saving enough to tide them over the end of the year," said a foreign bank dealer.
Another dealer said there were fewer lenders in the market because banks were squaring positions.
"They're investing in reverse repos and the Central Bank's special T-bills," he said.
In the secondary market for T-bills, buying was focussed on six-month and one-year bills because of their relatively attractive rates compared to the shorter-term bills where rates have fallen.
"We're still looking at the longer-term bills," said a dealer.
The six-month bills had bid rates rates ranging from 11.80 to 11.85 percent; and the one year had 12.10 to 12.30, dealers said.
